parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, no documented border profiling of trans visitors, and hate-crime protection in some regions are positives. But the dossier documents state-imposed universal-exposure measures: biological-sex interpretation of the equality act (April 2025), a statutory single-sex-spaces code in force with UN experts warning it institutionalises discrimination, strip-searching of trans women by officers of birth sex, custody/stop-and-search by biological sex, prison placement by birth sex upheld by courts, and a planned ban on trans patients in matching hospital wards. The Joelle case shows tier-1 harm in healthcare with unresolved recourse. Institutions here enforce the hostile rules, so rule of law is exposure, not mitigation. Hostile media climate and steep rights decline compound. Severity is capped (no arrest/imprisonment for being trans, no documented killings), keeping this out of High Risk, but state threat-framing plus universal exposures place it in Elevated Risk, upper half.
